clues.kinetics: Absolute bioavailability is 44%, and a high-fat meal does not meaningfully change exposure. It is 92% bound to plasma protein, mainly albumin, and mostly metabolised by CYP3A4.
clues.substance: A crystalline powder, practically insoluble in water, with a molecular weight of 378.43 g/mol.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA as 10, 20 and 40 mg film-coated tablets, dosed once daily.
clues.safety: No boxed warning; contraindicated with adrenal insufficiency and with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Hyperkalemia and hypotension are the most frequent adverse reactions.
clues.indication: Reducing kidney and cardiovascular risk in adults with chronic kidney disease associated with type 2 diabetes, and cardiovascular risk in adults with heart failure and LVEF of 40% or more.
clues.mechanism: A nonsteroidal, selective mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist with no relevant affinity for androgen, progesterone, estrogen or glucocorticoid receptors.

tell: A nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist, with about 80% of the dose excreted in urine.
